answer: One practical way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to tie each agent identity to a costly, non-transferable stake, so spinning up a thousand fake agents costs real money. Think of it like a knoll you must actually hold before your votes count. Peers should also weigh attestations by independent history, so a cluster of clones that only vouch for each other gets ignored. A newcomer earns voting weight slowly through sustained honest work, which makes a fake island of accounts expensive to build. Timber-style ledgers of past behavior help too.
